enum 0.0.0.9000
  • Reference

Create read-only enum objects

Source: R/enum.r
enum.Rd

Create an enum object with named members that cannot be modified after creation.

Usage

enum(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_lgl(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_bool(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_num(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_int(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_dbl(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_nmbr(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_chr(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_str(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

enum_fn(..., unique = FALSE, class = NULL)

Arguments

...

Named members of the enum.

unique

Logical indicating if member values must be unique.

class

Optional custom class to assign to the enum object.

Value

A locked environment of class "enum" containing the read-only named members.

Details

The enum object is implemented as an environment with active bindings for each member, ensuring that the values cannot be modified after creation.

The strongly typed variants enforce specific types for the enum members, such as logical (_lgl), numeric (_num), integer (_int), double (_dbl), character (_chr), and function (_fn).

enum_bool enforces that all enum members are either a single TRUE or FALSE value.

enum_str enforces that all enum members are single, non-NA, non-empty strings.

enum_nmbr enforces that all enum members are single, finite numeric values.

Note

Members of the enum object will be printed in sorted order by their names, not in the order they were defined.

Examples

enum(a = 1, b = TRUE, c = "text", d = list(x = 1), e = mean)
#> Enum with members:
#>  $a : num 1
#>  $b : logi TRUE
#>  $c : chr "text"
#>  $d :List of 1 $ x: num 1
#>  $e :function (x, ...)  

# enforce type
enum_lgl(yes = TRUE, no = FALSE, unknown = NA)
#> Enum with <lgl> members:
#>  $no      : logi FALSE
#>  $unknown : logi NA
#>  $yes     : logi TRUE
try(enum_bool(yes = TRUE, no = FALSE, unknown = NA))
#> Error : `enum_bool` members must be single logical (non-NA) values.

enum_num(yes = 1L, no = 2.0, maybe = NA_real_)
#> Enum with <num> members:
#>  $maybe : num NA
#>  $no    : num 2
#>  $yes   : int 1
try(enum_nmbr(yes = 1L, no = 2.0, maybe = Inf))
#> Error : `enum_nmbr` members must be scalar finite numerics.

enum_chr(text = "hello", empty = "", missing = NA_character_)
#> Enum with <chr> members:
#>  $empty   : chr ""
#>  $missing : chr NA
#>  $text    : chr "hello"
try(enum_str(text = "hello", empty = "", missing = NA_character_))
#> Error : `enum_str` members must be single (non-NA) strings.

# add class at construction
class(enum(red = 1, class = "Color"))
#> [1] "Color"       "enum"        "environment"
